summary: Hiralal Rasikdas Kapadia was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. In 1947, he was attested as Professor of Ardhamagadhi at MTB Arts College and as a University Teacher for the Ph.D. in Ardhamagadhi at the University of Mumbai.

Hiram W. Woodward is an art historian and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard and Yale, taught at Silpakorn University, the University of Michigan, and the University of Vermont, and served as curator at the Walters Art Museum (1986–2003).

Hirananda Sastri was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Dayanand Anglo-Vedic College and Oriental College. He held positions with the Archaeological Survey of India, the Government of India as Government Epigraphist, and served as Director of Archaeology for Baroda State (1934–1942).

Hirofumi Isoda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University by 1966. He served as a lecturer and associate professor at Tohoku University and is attested as professor emeritus at Shimane University.

Hirofumi Toda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a professor at Tokushima University from around 1970 to 2002 and was affiliated with the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

Hiroko Kawanami is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under John Okell and Anna J. Allott. Her career includes serving as a senior lecturer at Lancaster University, attested between 2013 and 2016.

Hiroko Matsuoka is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Hiroshima University and completed her Dr. phil. at the University of Leipzig. She has worked as research staff at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2021–2023) and the University of Vienna (2024).

Hiromasa Tosaki was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyushu and Harvard under Shōren Ihara, Satkari Mookerjee, and Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as a professor at Kyushu University from circa 1974 to 1994.

Hiromi Habata is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Freiburg. She held posts at the University of Munich, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Hiromi Yoshimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies. His career includes serving as a lecturer at Ryukoku University, where his affiliation is attested in 1987 and 2006.
Hiromichi Kato is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied as a graduate student under Ryogon Fukuhara. He served as a lecturer at Ryukoku University, attested in 1987.
Hiromitsu Ikuma is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from Tohoku University by 2019. He has held researcher posts at Taisho University and the Institute of Buzan Sectarian Studies.
Hiromu Kitanishi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied at Otani University. He later served as a professor at Otani University, attested in 1980.

Hironori Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Bukkyo University. He has held posts at Bukkyo University and Kyoto Bunkyo University, where he is attested as a lecturer in 2026.

Hironobu Minami is a Buddhist studies scholar. He has served as a research assistant at the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015) and as an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Hiroo Kashiwagi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo between ~1958 and 1963. He later served as a professor at Mie Chukyo University, attested in 1982.

Hiroo Sato is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University from ~1973 to 1981. He worked at Morioka College (~1989–1993) and served as a professor at Tohoku University (~2001–2019).

Hiroshi Aoyagi is a scholar of linguistics, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at International Christian University and earned his PhD at the University of Southern California, serving as a professor at Nanzan University in 1989.

Hiroshi Araki is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who earned his degrees, including a PhD, at Kyoto University. He taught at Aichi Prefectural University and Osaka University, and was a professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2010–2025).

Hiroshi Arami is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He is attested in 2026 as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
